chunks: ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Abū Muḥammad al-Isbāriqīnī, from ʿAlī ibn ʿAmr al-ʿAṭṭār, who said:

I entered upon Abū al-Ḥasan al-ʿAskarī (عليه السلام), while Abū Jaʿfar, his son, was still among the living, and I thought that he was the one. So I said to him: May I be sacrificed for you, which of your sons should I designate? He said: Do not designate anyone until my command comes out to you.
He said: I then wrote to him afterwards, asking in whom this matter would be. He wrote back to me: In the elder of my two sons. He said: And Abū Muḥammad was older than Abū Jaʿfar.

key_terms.أَخُصُّ: I single out or designate specifically
key_terms.أَمْرِي: my directive or command regarding the matter of authority
key_terms.الْكَبِيرِ: the elder, meaning the older one among the two sons
key_terms.هَذَا الْأَمْرُ: this matter, referring in context to the Imamate

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith indicate the succession among the sons of Abū al-Ḥasan al-ʿAskarī (عليه السلام)?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a question posed to Abū al-Ḥasan al-ʿAskarī (عليه السلام) regarding which of his sons should be singled out. The response postpones specification until his command is issued, and a later written reply indicates that the matter would be in the elder of his two sons. The report is significant in the context of identifying the succeeding Imam.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Abu Muhammad Al Isbariqeyni, from Ali Bin Amro Al Attar who said,

‘I went over to Abu Al-Hassan Al-Askary<sup>asws</sup> (10<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) and Abu Ja’far, his<sup>asws</sup> son during his life-time, and I thought that he would be him (the Imam<sup>asws</sup>). So I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! Whom from your<sup>asws</sup> sons should I choose?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do not choose anyone until my<sup>asws</sup> order comes out to you all’.

So I wrote to him<sup>asws</sup> afterwards, ‘In whom would this command (Imamate) come to be?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> wrote to me: ‘In the eldest of my<sup>asws</sup> sons’. And it was so that Abu Muhammad<sup>asws</sup> (11<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) was older than Abu Ja’far’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from abu Muhammad al-Asbarqiniy from Ali ibn ‘Amr al-‘Attar who has said the following. “Once I went to see al-Hassan al-‘Askari (a.s.) when his son abu Ja‘far (Muhammad ) was still alive and I thought he will be the Imam after his father. I then asked the Imam (a.s.), “May Allah take my souls in service for your cause, which of your sons I will consider (my Imam)?” The Imam (a.s.) said, “do not consider any of them (your Imam) until my command will come to you.”
The narrator has said, “I wrote to him afterwards asking, ‘To who will go this task (Leadership with Divine Authority)”
The narrator has said, “He wrote to me, “(It will go) to my eldest son.” The narrator has said, “Abu Muhammad (a.s.) was older then abu Ja‘far.”
